H("III. Governing Framework", 1)
P("Five CD provisions control how every gap below should be assessed:")
B("**The ROD controls (CD ¶14).** The ROD governs the scope, nature, and Performance Standards of the remedy. The order of precedence is CD, then ROD, then RAWP. “Performance Standards” expressly include the 1 mg/kg thermal treatment standard, all four groundwater cleanup levels, the ROD excavation depths and volumes, and the 30-year and 5-year RAO timeframes (CD ¶5(k)).")
B("**No self-executing deviations (CD ¶¶15, 21, 33).** A deviation needs prior written EPA approval through Section VII. Submitting a RAWP that proposes deviations “does not constitute authorization,” and implementing an ESD-level or Amendment-level change without completing that process is itself a violation.")
B("**The RAWP must implement every ROD element (CD ¶18(i)–(xi)).** This includes ARAR compliance demonstrations for all 47 ARARs (¶18(vii); ¶29).")
B("**Modification tiers (CD ¶32).** Minor Modifications cover operational details only. **ESD** changes include excavation-scope reductions above 10%, relaxed treatment standards, fewer extraction, injection, or monitoring wells, reduced monitoring frequency or coverage, and less protective containment-cell design. **ROD Amendment** changes include any cleanup-level change, elimination of a treatment technology (AOP is named expressly), and any change that causes the remedy to miss the ROD RAO timeframe. EPA classifies in its sole discretion (¶33).")
B("**Justification standard (CD ¶¶35–36).** A modification request must include a side-by-side comparison, data, modeling, pilot results, a protectiveness and ARAR assessment, a proposed classification, and cost and schedule impacts. “Vague or generalized assertions that a proposed modification is ‘functionally equivalent’ to or ‘consistent with’ the ROD requirement shall not constitute adequate technical justification.” The RAWP relies on precisely that phrasing for the 5 mg/kg standard (RAWP §§2.2, 3.3).")
P("On penalties, CD ¶49 sets **Major Deviations at $5,000/day**. These include failing to implement a required component, installing fewer wells than specified, building below ROD design specifications, and missing RAO timeframes. CD ¶51 sets **Minor Deviations at $1,500/day**. These include late deliverables, incorrect regulatory citations, incomplete ARAR matrices, missing certifications, haul-route deviations, and deficient ancillary plans. EPA may reclassify a Minor Deviation as Major if protectiveness is implicated (¶52). Penalties keep accruing during dispute resolution (¶56). Increased cost of performance is not force majeure (¶68).")
EOF

S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/environmental-esg/compare-remedial-action-work-plan-against-record-of-decision-requirements/claude-code-session/20261016-033457; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/p4.py <<"EOF"
s3 = doc.add_section(WD_SECTION.NEW_PAGE)
s3.orientation = WD_ORIENT.PORTRAIT
s3.page_width, s3.page_height = s3.page_height, s3.page_width
s3.left_margin = s3.right_margin = Inches(1)
H("V. Discussion of Principal Gaps", 1)
H("A. OU-3: the three ROD Amendment-level changes", 2)
P("**1,4-Dioxane cleanup level (Item 17).** The ROD set 0.35 µg/L deliberately. It identified the Health Advisory Level as a relevant and appropriate ARAR (Table 2-1, #4) and selected it over Ohio’s generic screening level because of the site-specific risk findings and the wellfield 1.8 miles downgradient (ROD §2.12.4). Ohio EPA, the agency whose “standard” the RAWP now invokes, commented in favor of 0.35 µg/L precisely because it is more stringent than the Ohio level (ROD §3.2.5). The CD repeats 0.35 µg/L four times (¶¶5(k)(ii), 24(b)(iii), 24(e), 98), including as a condition of termination. Any change to a cleanup level is a fundamental change requiring a ROD Amendment with public comment (CD ¶32(c); 40 C.F.R. § 300.435(c)(2)(ii)). A RAWP cannot make that change. EPA will almost certainly reject it, and the change would be the centerpiece of any public process the CAG has asked to join.")
P("**AOP omission (Item 18).** The treatment-train omission is the most indefensible gap on the record. The ROD’s alternatives analysis rejected pump-and-treat without AOP (OU-3 Alternative 3) because GAC and air stripping cannot meet 0.35 µg/L for 1,4-dioxane (ROD §2.9.3). The selected remedy includes AOP “specifically” for 1,4-dioxane and calls it “essential” (ROD §2.12.4). CD ¶32(c) names “elimination of advanced oxidation processes” as an example of a fundamental change, and CD ¶50 names “a treatment system that does not include a required technology component” as a Major Deviation. That deviation accrues from the day the plant becomes operational, at $5,000/day, until it is cured. The RAWP offers no bench, pilot, or vendor data that GAC will remove 1,4-dioxane. The two changes also reinforce each other: dropping AOP is only arguable at the 3.5 µg/L level, so both fall together. The CAG’s first question was whether AOP is included (CAG letter ¶3). The honest answer is that it is not.")
P("**45-year timeframe (Item 23).** The RAWP itself projects that groundwater RAOs will take about 45 years (§13.2), while restating the 30-year standard in §2.1. A remedy designed to miss the RAO timeframe is a fundamental change (CD ¶32(c)). Missing the 30-year timeframe is also a Major Deviation in its own right (CD ¶¶30, 49(v)). The RAWP also moves the start of the clock from “initial system startup” (ROD §2.8) to “full-scale system operation,” which is a further unapproved change. In effect, the RAWP’s own model shows the cumulative effect of the OU-1 source-removal reductions (Items 1, 5, 6) and the OU-3 reductions (Items 19, 21). It is evidence against the RAWP, not support for it.")
H("B. OU-3: hydraulic containment and wellfield protection", 2)
P("Wellfield protection is the ROD’s primary driver (ROD §§2.1, 2.7.1, 3.2.3). The ROD requires capture of the full plume width plus 200 feet on each side. On the ROD and RAWP plume dimensions (0.4 mile ≈ 2,112 ft), that is roughly 2,500 feet of capture. The RAWP’s 2,000-foot alignment is shorter than the plume itself. It also substitutes discrete wells for the ROD’s extraction trench, drops quarterly capture-zone verification, and rests the capture demonstration on an updated model (App. I). That model uses hydrogeologic parameters that differ markedly from the ROD: saturated thickness of 25–40 ft against 8–12 ft, and a geometric-mean K of about 4×10⁻³ cm/s (≈11 ft/day) against 28 ft/day. The model is not described in the PDI memo, whose scope was limited to OU-1 and OU-2. Together with the 28-well network, semi-annual-only sampling, and a possible move to annual sampling, the design has less capture margin and less early-warning capability than the ROD requires. The proposed extraction-well depths of 30–45 ft also need engineering scrutiny. On the ROD’s stratigraphy, wells that deep may penetrate the clay aquitard that separates the shallow plume from the bedrock aquifer serving the wellfield (ROD §2.5.1). If EPA reads the design that way, it is a protectiveness issue, not a cost issue.")
H("C. OU-1: source removal and SEE", 2)
P("The PDI data do not support a uniform 12-ft excavation. Five of the twelve borings, clustered over the central and eastern DNAPL area, exceed industrial PRGs at 13.5–15.0 ft. Some exceed by multiples: Cr(VI) at 42 mg/kg is about 7× the PRG, and TCE at 18 mg/kg is about 5.6× the PRG. Terraverde’s memo recommends keeping 15 ft as the default and reducing to 12 ft only where confirmation sampling at the 12-ft horizon is clean (PDI §5.1). The RAWP presents the PDI’s 38,200-cy “blended” volume while specifying a uniform 12-ft maximum, so the volume and the design do not match. Because the RAWP’s volume reduction (9.0%) is just under the 10% ESD trigger in CD ¶32(b), CCH may be tempted to argue that no ESD is needed. We do not recommend that argument. Depth is an independent Performance Standard (CD ¶5(k)(iii)). The ROD sets 15 ft as a **minimum** across OU-1. The ¶32(b) examples are “without limitation.” And EPA alone decides the classification (¶33). Even the PDI’s variable-depth approach departs from the ROD’s “minimum 15 ft” language. It should go to EPA as a formal ¶35 request, not be built into a RAWP.")
P("On SEE, the RAWP reduces the well pairs to 12 and the source zone to 1.5 acres. The ROD says 3.5 acres; the PDI says 2.8 acres. Those reductions contradict the ROD’s “shall maintain the minimum of 14” and the PDI’s explicit advice. The pilot data also suggest a further engineering question that cuts against any reduction. At the observed 10–15-ft effective radii, 12 or even 14 single-injector pairs would heat only a small fraction of a 1.5–3.5-acre zone (about 0.15 acre at a 12-ft radius). Either the full-scale design depends on details not stated in the RAWP text (App. C), or the source zone is under-designed even at 14 pairs. Either way, there is no basis to go below the ROD minimum.")
P("The 5 mg/kg thermal standard is a relaxed treatment standard, an ESD-level change (CD ¶32(b)). Its only justification is “functionally equivalent,” which CD ¶36 expressly rejects. The ROD applies 1 mg/kg “regardless of intended reuse” to prevent recontamination of the subsurface (ROD §2.12.2). The RAWP also treats only VOC-impacted soils and screens backfill only for VOCs. As a result, soils excavated because they exceed the Cr(VI), PCP, or BaP PRGs, which LTTD does not reliably address (Cr(VI) in particular), could be placed back in the excavation. That gap should be closed regardless of the treatment-standard issue.")
H("D. OU-2: lagoon removal and containment cell", 2)
P("The RAWP’s 10-ft excavation is the PDI’s “not recommended” comparison scenario. A 10-ft cut leaves 1.5–3.0 ft of contaminated material on top of the clay at every boring and defeats RAO OU-2-1, which is to prevent migration from lagoon materials to groundwater. The 15.4% volume reduction exceeds the CD’s 10% ESD threshold on its face. The liner change from 60-mil/24-in. to 40-mil/18-in. contradicts the ROD, CD ¶23(b), and Pinnacle’s recommendation. CD ¶50 specifically lists “a containment cell constructed with a liner system that does not meet ROD specifications” as a continuing Major Deviation. The RAWP’s statement that the reduced liner satisfies 40 CFR 264.310 does not cure the problem, because the ROD and CD set the specification independently of the ARAR. Sending leachate to the Millhaven POTW replaces a ROD-specified remedy component, reverses the ROD’s ARAR finding that the site would not discharge to a POTW (Table 2-1, #34), and adds an off-site pretreatment-permit dependency that the ROD avoided. The 30,000-cy cell is sized to the reduced excavation. It must be re-sized for the full ROD volume, bulking, and any OU-4 soils CCH elects to consolidate (CD ¶25(a)).")
H("E. OU-4: riparian corridor", 2)
P("The RAWP keeps the 3-ft depth and appropriately schedules work for July–October, outside the April–June spawning restriction. However, it reduces the volume by 13.2%, attributing the reduction to PDI data that do not appear in the PDI memo. It also drops ODNR as co-approver of the Habitat Restoration Plan, shortens monitoring from five to three years, thins surface-water monitoring after Year 1, substitutes Ohio EPA benthic protocols for the RI protocols and reference stations required for a valid before-and-after comparison, and makes contingency planting discretionary. Each change is contrary to ROD §2.12.5 and CD ¶25. Several of them (ODNR approval, the 5-year program) were specifically endorsed by Ohio EPA in its ROD comments (ROD §3.2.5).")
EOF
echo ok'

S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/environmental-esg/compare-remedial-action-work-plan-against-record-of-decision-requirements/claude-code-session/20261016-033457; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/p5.py <<"EOF"
H("VI. Cross-Cutting Requirements", 1)
H("A. Community Air Monitoring and Haul Route", 2)
P("These two items carry outsized enforcement and reputational risk because they were explicit commitments in EPA’s Responsiveness Summary (ROD §3.2.2), and the CAG has already raised both with EPA. Doubling the VOC fenceline trigger to 10 ppmv contradicts the ROD and CD ¶26. Under the CD, CAMP deficiencies are Minor Deviations ($1,500/day, ¶51(v)), but EPA may reclassify any deviation that “has the potential to compromise … the protection of human health” (¶52). A relaxed VOC trigger next to homes with children and asthmatic residents (CAG letter ¶4) is a likely candidate. The CAMP also omits OU-3 intrusive work (trenching, well drilling, injections), places stations at the work-area perimeter rather than the fenceline, has no CAG reporting, and does not reference the NYSDOH guidance named in CD ¶26.")
P("The County Road 12 route violates ROD §2.12.6 and CD ¶27, which require State Route 47 to I-71 and forbid any routing through Millhaven Heights. The RAWP’s only justification is directness (§10.1). CD ¶51(iii) classifies route deviations as Minor, but each truck day would be a separate day of non-compliance, and the facts the CAG cites (a daycare, an elementary school, a narrow road, hundreds of loads) make reclassification under ¶52 realistic. Separately, the RAWP routes trucks “south on County Road 12” from Old Mill Road, whereas the ROD describes Old Mill Road as connecting to SR-47 about 0.5 mile **north** (ROD §2.1). The ROD-compliant route appears to be readily available.")
H("B. Health and Safety Plan", 2)
P("CD ¶28 and ROD §2.12.6 require a HASP compliant with 29 CFR 1910.120. The RAWP and Appendix H cite 29 CFR 1926.65. The two standards are substantively parallel, but CD ¶51(ii) expressly treats “incorrect regulatory citations in plans” as a Minor Deviation. The fix is trivial and should be made. The RAWP summary also does not describe the 40-hour/8-hour HAZWOPER training, the exclusion/contamination-reduction/support zones, or decontamination procedures that the ROD and CD ¶28 call for. Appendix H is also described as both the HASP and the Community Notification Plan (RAWP §§9.3, 11.1). That labeling should be corrected.")
H("C. ARARs Crosswalk", 2)
P("CD ¶¶18(vii) and 29 require a compliance demonstration for **each** of the 47 ROD ARARs. RAWP Table 12-1 lists 39 requirements and gives only a one-line “applicability” entry for each. The crosswalk below compares the RAWP against ROD Table 2-1.")
T(["Status", "ROD ARARs (Table 2-1 No.)", "Comment"], [

input.command:
S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/environmental-esg/compare-remedial-action-work-plan-against-record-of-decision-requirements/claude-code-session/20261016-033457; $S $R 'cat > /workspace/build/p6.py <<"EOF"
H("VII. RAWP vs. PDI Memorandum: Inconsistencies, Certification, and Privilege", 1)
P("The RAWP says that “PDI results support optimization of certain remedy components” (§1.4) and repeatedly invokes the PDI to justify reductions. The PDI memo, however, is signed by the same engineer who certified the RAWP, and it recommends ROD-conforming design on every OU-1 and OU-2 issue it addresses:")
T(["Issue", "PDI memo (Oct. 15, 2024)", "RAWP (Dec. 20, 2024)"], [
 ["OU-1 depth", "Keep 15 ft as the design basis; a blanket 12 ft leaves contamination in about 42% of the investigated area (§5.1)", "12 ft maximum; “optimized” from the ROD (§3.1)"],
 ["SEE well pairs", "14; “do not recommend adopting 12 … absent” full-scale data, and none has been collected (§§3.3, 5.1, 6)", "12 (§3.2)"],
 ["DNAPL zone", "≈2.8 acres (§3.2)", "≈1.5 acres (§3.2)"],
 ["Thermal standard", "“The RAWP should incorporate the ROD-specified standard of 1 mg/kg” (§5.1)", "5 mg/kg (§3.3)"],
 ["OU-2 depth", "To the clay (11.5–13.0 ft); 10 ft “not recommended” (§§4.3, 5.2)", "10 ft (§4.1)"],
 ["Liner", "60-mil/24-in.; “no technical basis … for reducing” (§§4.2, 5.2)", "40-mil/18-in. (§4.2)"],
 ["OU-2 wells", "8 (§5.2)", "6 (§4.4)"],
 ["PDI scope", "21 borings (12 at OU-1, 9 at OU-2); 10 temporary well points; 2 SEE pilot tests; OU-1 and OU-2 only; field work June 3–Sept. 20, 2024", "42 borings; 186 samples; 8 temporary monitoring wells; 4 groundwater rounds from 32 wells; aquifer pumping tests; OU-4 sampling; Feb.–Aug. 2024; PDI Work Plan submitted July 2024 (§§1.4, 6.1)"],
 ["Project / license nos.", "Project TVE-2024-0387; P.E. License No. PE-68245", "Project TVE-2024-0347; Ohio P.E. Registration No. 67842"],
 ["CD entry date", "Entered March 12, 2020", "Entered “March 2020” (ROD §2.2: lodged March 12, entered April 28, 2020)"],
], [1.3, 2.7, 2.5], size=8)
P("**Implications.** First, the RAWP’s characterization of the PDI is inaccurate in material respects. CCH must certify every deliverable “under penalty of law” as “true, accurate, and complete” (CD ¶47). No such certification appears in the RAWP, and none could responsibly be given for it in its current form. Second, the RAWP states that the PDI Summary Memorandum “was submitted to EPA on October 15, 2024,” with data in Appendix A. If that is accurate, any privilege over the memo has likely been waived, and EPA already has a CCH document rebutting the RAWP. If it is not accurate, the RAWP misstates the record. Third, even if the memo’s opinions remain privileged, CD ¶¶79–80 require CCH to provide all analytical data, field notes, and contractor reports relating to the Work within 30 days and bar privilege claims over Work data. The underlying boring data (e.g., the 13.5–15 ft exceedances, the 11.5–13.0 ft clay contacts, and the pilot-test radii) are therefore discoverable by and deliverable to EPA in any event. We should confirm immediately what was actually transmitted to EPA and when.")
P("**Other internal defects** that EPA is likely to flag: the plant figure is cited to Appendix J in §7.1 but to Appendix B in the figure list. Appendix N is cited both as the QAPP and as the cost worksheets. The site description differs from the ROD: the RAWP places the Site in “southeastern” rather than western Ashford County, describes agricultural rather than industrial land to the north, and places the lagoons in the southern rather than southwestern portion. The RAWP states the ROD was signed by the Regional Administrator, when the signatories were the RPM and the Acting RA. The RAWP gives the EPA review period as Jan. 28–Mar. 28, 2025. Sixty days from the Jan. 15 submission is March 16, 2025, or March 17 under CD ¶5(d)’s weekend rule. Sixty days from Jan. 28 is March 29. The date of EPA’s receipt should be confirmed.")
P("**Anomalies in the governing documents themselves.** The CD as provided is dated as entered in 2020, yet it recites and incorporates the September 15, 2021 ROD. It also contains several recitals that conflict with the ROD, including: maximum TCE of 18,400 µg/L against the ROD’s 4,800 µg/L; OU-2 in the “southeastern” portion of the Site; a plume running “northwesterly”; and a May 15–July 15, 2021 comment period with a June 10 meeting, against the ROD’s June 15–July 30 and June 28. It also refers to the ROD’s ARAR matrix as “Table 12” (the ROD calls it Table 2-1). Under CD ¶14 and ¶12, the ROD’s technical content would control. Before we take positions with EPA that depend on dates (RAWP timeliness, the financial-assurance deadline), we should obtain the entered, file-stamped CD and any amendments.")

H("VIII. Procedural Compliance and Stipulated-Penalty Exposure", 1)
T(["Exposure category", "Items", "Rate / trigger", "Illustration"], [
 ["Major Deviations (design/technology)", "Items 1, 5, 8, 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22, 23 (and potentially 25, 27)", "$5,000/day per deviation (¶49). For design/operational deficiencies, accrual runs from the date the deficient component becomes operational until cured (¶50)", "$1.825M per deviation-year. Thirteen concurrent deviations for one year ≈ $23.7M. **Avoidable** if the RAWP is conformed before construction (RA may not begin before approval, ¶21)"],
 ["Major Deviation (timeframe)", "Item 23 (45 vs. 30 years)", "¶¶30, 49(v)", "Accrues on failure to meet the RAO timeframe; it also undermines the covenant not to sue (¶72) and termination (¶¶95, 98)"],
 ["Minor Deviation: late RAWP", "Item 35", "$1,500/day (¶51(i)) from the 36-month deadline (¶17)", "From Apr. 28, 2023: 628 days ≈ $942,000. From Mar. 12, 2023: 675 days ≈ $1,012,500. Subject to any EPA-granted extension, which should be confirmed"],
 ["Minor Deviations: plan/administrative", "Items 29, 31, 32, 34 (citations, ARAR matrix, certification, CAMP/HASP)", "$1,500/day each (¶51(ii), (v)); arguably accruing from submission", "≈$547,500 per deviation-year. EPA may reclassify CAMP and haul-route items as Major (¶52)"],
 ["Minor Deviation: haul route", "Item 30", "$1,500/day (¶51(iii)) per day of non-compliant hauling", "Prospective only; high reclassification risk"],
], [1.4, 1.6, 1.9, 1.6], size=8)
P("Penalties continue to accrue during dispute resolution (¶56). EPA’s RAWP decisions are reviewed under the deferential arbitrary-and-capricious standard (¶63). Questions of how to interpret the ROD are reviewed de novo (¶64). Neither standard gives CCH a meaningful litigation path on the core items: the ROD and CD text is explicit on every number at issue. The cost of performance is not force majeure (¶68). Material non-performance also puts the covenant not to sue at risk (¶¶72, 74(i), (iv)) and exposes CCH to a UAO or EPA performance of the Work with cost recovery (¶¶74, 76).")

H("IX. CAG Concerns: Verification Against the Record", 1)
T(["CAG concern (Feb. 5, 2025 letter)", "Finding", "Record basis"], [
 ["Overall scope reduced; cost “significantly lower”", "**Confirmed.** $72.1M vs. $89.4M; most design minimums reduced", "Part IV; RAWP §14.1; ROD §2.14"],
 ["AOP for 1,4-dioxane may not be included", "**Confirmed.** AOP omitted; GAC relied upon", "RAWP §7.1; ROD §2.12.4; CD ¶24(b)(iii)"],
 ["Cleanup levels may not match the ROD", "**Confirmed for 1,4-dioxane** (3.5 vs. 0.35 µg/L); TCE, PCE, and Cr(VI) match", "RAWP Table 2-1; ROD §2.12.4"],
 ["CAMP thresholds may differ", "**Confirmed for VOCs** (10 vs. 5 ppmv); PM-10 matches", "RAWP Table 9-1; ROD §2.12.6"],
 ["Haul route may be County Road 12", "**Confirmed**", "RAWP §10.1, Fig. 10-1; ROD §2.12.6; CD ¶27"],
 ["Reduced depths, fewer wells, weaker monitoring", "**Confirmed** across OU-1 through OU-4", "Items 1–27"],
 ["Wellfield protection", "**Concern well-founded.** Extraction capture width, network size, and frequency reduced; AOP removed; 45-year timeline", "Items 17–23"],
 ["Notice and comment on any ESD/ROD Amendment; public meeting", "A ROD Amendment requires public notice and comment (40 C.F.R. § 300.435(c)(2)(ii); CD ¶5(q)). An ESD requires public notice and placement in the Administrative Record but no formal comment period (§ 300.435(c)(2)(i)). EPA is very likely to involve the CAG", "CD ¶¶5(h), 5(q), 32"],
], [2.0, 2.6, 1.9], size=8)
P("Practically, any attempt to carry the three fundamental changes forward would go through a ROD Amendment, and the CAG has positioned itself to oppose it. Given Ohio EPA’s documented support for 0.35 µg/L and AOP (ROD §3.2.5), the prospects for such an amendment are poor.")
EOF
echo ok'

The RAWP, as submitted, does not implement the ROD. Measured line-by-line against the ROD and the Consent Decree (CD), it departs from the selected remedy on **at least 30 discrete requirements**, and nearly every departure runs in the same direction: less excavation, fewer wells, thinner liners, weaker standards, less monitoring, and lower cost. None of these departures was submitted through the CD Section VII modification process, and none is supported by an ESD or ROD Amendment. Under CD ¶14 the ROD controls over the RAWP, and under CD ¶¶15 and 33 a RAWP that proposes deviations does not authorize them. EPA's approval would not cure the problem either (CD ¶40).

The most serious findings are:

- **Three changes that the CD itself classifies as "fundamental" and that require a ROD Amendment with public comment (CD ¶32(c)):** (1) the 1,4-dioxane cleanup level is raised tenfold, from 0.35 µg/L to 3.5 µg/L (RAWP §§2.2, 5.4); (2) the UV/hydrogen peroxide advanced oxidation process (AOP) unit is removed from the treatment train, and the RAWP relies on GAC for 1,4-dioxane, which the ROD found technically ineffective (RAWP §7.1; ROD §§2.9.3, 2.12.4); and (3) the groundwater restoration timeframe is projected at about 45 years, against a 30-year Performance Standard (RAWP §13.2; ROD §2.8; CD ¶¶5(k), 30).
